findings.description: The instance user-data script embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. User data is retrievable by principals with instance metadata/configuration access and is commonly persisted in Terraform state or source control, exposing reusable credentials.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Unless account-level default EBS encryption is independently enforced, this creates an unencrypted volume and leaves its data readable from underlying storage or derived artifacts.

This snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage, which is not configured for encryption. EBS snapshots inherit the source volume's encryption state, so this snapshot can contain the volume data without encryption at rest.
Ingress TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. Any Internet host can attempt administrative access to instances using this security group, enabling broad password/key-guessing and exploit attempts.

Ingress TCP/80 is exposed to 0.0.0.0/0, and the attached instance installs and serves Apache HTTP content with no TLS listener or HTTPS configuration shown. Clients can therefore communicate with the service in cleartext and are susceptible to interception or modification in transit.

The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress network controls for the Internet-reachable host, facilitating data exfiltration or attacker command-and-control after compromise.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances. This subnet is also routed to an Internet gateway, and web_host is deployed into it with Internet-open security-group rules, making the host directly reachable from untrusted networks.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to every instance launched in this subnet. Its associated route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 through the Internet gateway, creating a public network segment rather than a private workload subnet.
